name: Iran

campaign_state.basis: Strikes on energy facilities in Iran were reported in 2025 and in 2026. No ceasefire or end is reported.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on the date checked. A search that returns no recent report does not show that none occurred. Iteration 20 added four conflict-level searches (the wider war, the Gulf states as a group, Iraq). None reported an end of the war, and renewed hostilities were reported in the autumn of 2026. No facility was looked up.

no_index_reason: Only the Russia-theatre system has a disruption index. Its weights and recovery assumptions were designed for that theatre and are not transferred to other countries, so this page shows reported disruptions and national energy context instead. No index is not a zero.

sectors.reason: Only a national total was read (EIA estimate, early 2024), and crude distillation and condensate splitting are quoted on different bases. No per-refinery table was read: the refining company's posted yearbooks stop at 2018-19 and other official sites could not be opened. Not scored.

sectors.reason: No current plant list or national installed capacity was read: the power holding company's site could not be opened, and the one cached list ends in 2015. The system runs a standing seasonal shortfall, so there is no undisrupted baseline to score against. Not scored.

sectors.reason: No regional inventory or event stream; the event-burden measure does not fit, and grid topology is outside what this project collects.
sectors.label: Transmission burden

sectors.reason: Small but not zero: EIA reports coal at 0.3% of primary energy production in 2022 and no coal-fired generation. A mine inventory is not yet researched.
sectors.label: Coal

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is reported under wartime restrictions by the authorities concerned, so independent, attacker-side and open-source reporting carry most of the record.
reporting_note: A war involving attacks on Iranian territory is recorded from 28 February 2026, after an earlier one in June 2025, and each party restricts what is reported about damage. Most Iranian official and agency sites could not be read from outside the country when this was written. No record has been published for Iran yet: the searches so far found ministry statements carried by state-supervised news agencies, and no body publishes an event register, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: 31 provinces (ostan), the official count since Alborz was created in 2010. Codes are the current ISO 3166-2 numbering (IR-00 to IR-30). Natural Earth, the map source, still carries the numbering from before November 2020, in which all but two codes meant a different province, so its shapes are moved to the current codes by province name. Boundaries are Natural Earth's default edition, which is an analytic and cartographic choice, not a statement about sovereignty. Offshore installations lie outside every province. Electricity is organised by regional companies, not by these provinces.

rulings.note: Fars. Natural Earth carries the numbering from before 2020, in which this code meant Tehran. This system uses the current numbering throughout.

Yazd. Drawn on an older extent: Natural Earth marks the subdivision of the former Khorasan province as estimated, and the Tabas area, which current sources place in South Khorasan, is drawn inside Yazd. A statement about the map file.

Hormozgan. At this map's level of detail none of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs is drawn. Iran administers the three islands and the United Arab Emirates claims them. Natural Earth's source file attaches Abu Musa to this province, which is a property of the map file and not a statement about sovereignty. The islands are never a unit of analysis and no event is placed on them.

South Khorasan. Drawn on an older extent: Natural Earth marks the subdivision of the former Khorasan province as estimated, and the Tabas area, which current sources place in South Khorasan, is drawn inside Yazd. A statement about the map file.
Alborz. Natural Earth gives Alborz the same code as Tehran. It has been a separate province since 2010 and is a separate unit here, under its current ISO code.

precision_policy.reason: Strikes on energy facilities in Iran are being reported now. While that holds, an attack or sabotage record is recorded for the country, with no province, facility or operator: a province and a class would often name the site. Other events (accidents, weather, grid failures) are placed by province.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Iran source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read on the cited page in this session. All ten come from one source, the U.S. EIA country analysis brief last updated 2024-10-10, so vintages are 2022 to early 2024 and predate the June 2025 and 2026 conflicts: they describe the system before those events and say nothing about its present state. Several are EIA estimates and are labelled so. Iranian official sites (Ministry of Petroleum, Ministry of Energy, Tavanir, Statistical Center of Iran) could not be read on this date, OPEC, IEA and the Energy Institute refused scripted access, and Iran has submitted no JODI-Oil data since July 2018, so no figure is taken from any of them. National installed generating capacity was not read on any page and is deliberately absent. See docs/countries/IR_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: Natural gas made up 55.7% of Iran's primary energy production in 2022 and petroleum and other liquids 43.4% (EIA).
Natural gas supplied 67.6% of Iran's primary energy consumption and 85.2% of its electricity generation in 2022 (EIA).
Iran produced 9.4 trillion cubic feet of dry natural gas in 2023 and consumed 8.9 trillion cubic feet (EIA).
Iran produced 4.0 million barrels per day of petroleum and other liquids in 2023, of which almost 2.9 million barrels per day was crude oil (EIA).
EIA estimated Iran's proved natural gas reserves at 1,200 trillion cubic feet as of December 2023.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: The citations of this system have not been link-checked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
